title: Malaysia unveils 6 homegrown chips from its semiconductor design park
source_used: EdgeProp (The Edge group), Kuala Lumpur, 16 Oct 2026
key_facts: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir launched six chips on Friday 16 Oct 2026, developed under the Semiconductor IC Design Park.
Combined estimated sales potential is RM300 million; he did not say when it could be reached.

The six: SkyeChip's MARS1000 AI processor; MaiStorage's aiDAPTIV+ storage for AI computers and servers; SiliconX's FPGA; Infinecs' automotive power regulator; Weeroc Space's power controller for satellites; Alphaswift's FC Mini drone flight controller.
Malaysia opened its first IC design park in Puchong in August 2024 and a second in Cyberjaya in November 2025.
Akmal said Malaysia must move from manufacturing products designed elsewhere to designing, developing and owning its technologies.
The National Semiconductor Strategy targets 110 high-value Malaysian semiconductor companies (10 existing, 100 new).
quote_evidence: Malaysia’s six homegrown semiconductor innovations developed under the Semiconductor IC Design Park have an estimated combined sales potential of RM300 million, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
However, he did not specify when the sales target could be achieved.
Akmal said Malaysia must move beyond manufacturing products locally to designing, developing and owning its own technologies.
why_it_matters_hint: Malaysia, long an assembly and testing hub, is trying to win chip design work.
